**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The IP architecture in Article X works in our favour:

- **Ownership split.** Program Inventions are allocated across Sanofi Sole, RevMed Sole and Joint buckets (Section 10.1(a); defs. 1.103, 1.109). Nothing in the Agreement assigns Sanofi background IP, know-how or funded data to RevMed.
- **Joint ownership is exploitable.** Section 10.1(b) gives each Party the right to exploit and license Joint Program Technology "without a duty of accounting or any obligation to seek consent," with a perpetual, irrevocable, fully-paid, worldwide, sublicensable licence to effect that outside the US — and RevMed's interest remains subject to Sanofi's exclusive licences. That clears the walk-away test (joint ownership *without* unrestricted exploitation) and meets the preferred position.
- **Third parties/subcontractors.** Must assign Program Inventions to the engaging Party (10.1(a)); post-signing subcontractors must assign or grant an irrevocable, perpetual, fully-paid, exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide sublicensable licence (p0259).
- **Data and regulatory assets flow to us.** RevMed "hereby does assign" all Regulatory Approvals, INDs and NDAs to Sanofi on completion of its Clinical Trials (Section 6.2); Sanofi owns Product Marks and domains (10.5), controls prosecution of the Sanofi Prosecuted Patents (10.2(a)) and holds sole enforcement rights for Product Infringement (10.4(b)).
- **Licence back to RevMed is narrow.** Section 3.2 is non-exclusive, royalty-free and limited to performing RevMed's obligations.

One item noted in the rationale rather than flagged: the operative allocation sentence in Section 10.1(a) is redacted (`[***]`) in this copy, so the precise Sanofi/RevMed/joint split should be verified against the unredacted text before signature.
